subject: Legend for discrete variable with many levels

messages.author: 637c00088bba8c56
messages.subject: Legend for discrete variable with many levels
parts:
Dear,

I have a plot with clusters of patients (factor with 7 levels, mapped
to color) and their location (factor with 171 levels, mapped to size).
Right now I'm supressing the size legend, as it doesn't fit on the
same viewport as the plot itself. Can I somehow include it, without
obscuring the plot (like on a different viewport fro example) ? My
code so far:


p <- ggplot(mdsdata2d)
p <- p + geom_point(aes(x = coord1, y = coord2, colour = patient, size
= location), shape = 1)

my_scale_size <- scale_size_manual(values = seq(1, 6, length.out =
171))
my_scale_size$legend <- FALSE #supressing size legend

p <- p + my_scale_size
p <- p + geom_vline(aes(x = 0), linetype = 2) + geom_hline(aes(x = 0),
linetype = 2)
p <- p + xlab("Coordinate 1") + ylab("Coordinate 2")
print(p)

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: Legend for discrete variable with many levels
parts:
Hi,
I think you need to consider what information you want to convey. With
171 sizes, viewers are not going to be able to distinguish the 10th
size from the 11th, or probably even the 10th form the 20th. If they
are ordered you can simply treat location as a continuous variable. If
not, probably mapping any aesthetic to this variable will not produce
very good results. You could instead use facet_wrap to show small
multiples across the 171 levels.

Best,
Ista

Thanks for Your replies. Points taken, though the location variable
really means coded discrete locations (as if nothing in common, no
particular order etc), so I believe cannot be treated as continuous or
even semi-continuous. The only reason I even consider mapping them to
sizes is outlier detection - every patient type has the same set of
locations recorded, would be insightful to inspect whether the same
locations are outlying in patient clusters.

I was thinking about creating 1 by 2 view-port (1 row, two columns)
and plotting bubble plot on the left with legend for color mapping
only, then only the sizes legend on the second view-port - how can I
extract the legend from the plot though?

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Legend for discrete variable with many levels
parts:
I think I understand better, but I'm still not sure how you're really going to compare things. 

If I understand correctly, each patient has a value for a series of 171 locations, and you want to be able to compare the patient data at each location relative to the distribution of the points.  Because you want to look at the distribution of the points and compare locations simultaneously you cannot simply facet the data in chunks.  

I suppose you could plot all the points by color with a very small different type of point, then layer on top of that a subset of the locations. 

Something like...
ggplot(aes(x = coord1, y = coord2, colour=patient))+
geom_point(data = mdsdata2d, size=0.5, shape = 3)+
geom_point(data = droplevels(subset(mdsdata2d, location = 1:10)), aes(size=location))+
geom_vline(aes(x = 0), linetype = 2) +
geom_hline(aes(x = 0), linetype = 2) +

xlab("Coordinate 1") +
ylab("Coordinate 2")

#untested since I don't have a dataset to play with
#I'm really not sure if that subset call with work, 
# I've never tried a range before. 

The only other thing I could think of is mean-centering your patient x and y coordinates and comparing the coordinates of your locations... cum grano salis, IANAS.

B

messages.subject: Re: Legend for discrete variable with many levels
parts:
Many thanks for Your help, I think I will settle for geom_text with
plotted location names as labels. I have tried Your code, the problem
is exacly the same as I had from beginning, namely when using size
mapped to location variable without supressing the legend it obscures
the whole plot (all you can actually see is one big dot). If you use
scale manual then still the label doesn't fit the plot, too many
levels, you're gonna see just the middle values. Subsetting works like
charm though.

Anyway I'm satisfied with the way it looks now, thank you all once
again for helping.

On Apr 4, 4:36 pm, Brandon Hurr <brandon.h...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I think I understand better, but I'm still not sure how you're really going
> to compare things.
>
> If I understand correctly, each patient has a value for a series of 171
> locations, and you want to be able to compare the patient data at each
> location relative to the distribution of the points.  Because you want to
> look at the distribution of the points and compare locations simultaneously
> you cannot simply facet the data in chunks.
>
> I suppose you could plot all the points by color with a very small different
> type of point, then layer on top of that a subset of the locations.
>
> Something like...
> ggplot(aes(x = coord1, y = coord2, colour=patient))+
> geom_point(data = mdsdata2d, size=0.5, shape = 3)+
> geom_point(data = droplevels(subset(mdsdata2d, location = 1:10)),
> aes(size=location))+
> geom_vline(aes(x = 0), linetype = 2) +
> geom_hline(aes(x = 0), linetype = 2) +
> xlab("Coordinate 1") +
> ylab("Coordinate 2")
>
> #untested since I don't have a dataset to play with
> #I'm really not sure if that subset call with work,
> # I've never tried a range before.
>
> The only other thing I could think of is mean-centering your patient x and y

> coordinates and comparing the coordinates of your locations... *cum grano
> salis*, IANAS.
>
> B

>
> On Mon, Apr 4, 2011 at 14:47, bulva <fbiele...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Please take a look at the plot produced with my previous code, should
> > become clearer at what am I aiming to (a readable label for size

> > contained

> > > If you could provide a self-contained example of what you currently have
